items.headline: Claude Haiku 5.5 launches at about one-tenth of the old price
items.summary: Anthropic released Haiku 5.5, its smallest and fastest model, at $0.10 per million input tokens (a token is roughly a word fragment) versus $1.00 for Haiku 4.5. It adds an adjustable effort setting and is built for high-volume jobs like summaries and sorting.
items.why_it_matters: If you use tools or automations built on Claude, cheaper and faster models like this tend to lower your bills and speed up customer-facing chat and workflows.

items.headline: Claude Sonnet 5.5 is faster and better at slides and spreadsheets
items.summary: Sonnet 5.5, the everyday Claude model, writes more than 30% faster than Sonnet 5, uses fewer tokens per task, and has a stronger design sense for documents, slides, and spreadsheets. Price is unchanged at $2 / $10 per million tokens.
items.why_it_matters: It is the model most people get in the Claude apps, so everyday writing and deck work should feel quicker and more polished without costing more.

opportunity.angle: I put Claude Sonnet 5.5 through real small-business work so you can see what actually changed

items.headline: Anthropic puts $100 million into training 10,000 Claude engineers
items.summary: Anthropic announced the Claude Frontier Academy, a residency program to train 10,000 engineers to roll out Claude inside companies by the end of 2027, with Accenture, Deloitte, and McKinsey among launch partners.
items.why_it_matters: It signals how fast big businesses are adopting Claude, and that hands-on help for small teams to adopt it is likely to grow too.
